last_digest.rss_summary: The supply chain attack campaign's shift toward developer endpoints and cloud access signals what could be next for the cybercrime outfit.

last_digest.rss_summary:

Breach notification service Have I Been Pwned (HIBP) added the data to its database on 27 October, listing email addresses and email messages as the compromised information. last_digest.rss_summary: Hackers stole passport numbers, frequent flyer numbers, email addresses and phone numbers for about 2,000 customers.

last_week_digest.title: Nikkei data breach affected over 1.8 million records
last_week_digest.tldr: Nikkei recently suffered a data breach involving 1.83 million records after attackers exploited stolen credentials to access a cloud development environment. While financial data remained secure, the incident highlights persistent vulnerabilities in third-party cloud services. This event signals that enterprises must prioritise rigorous credential management to mitigate escalating global cyber risks.

last_week_digest.title: FBI says SafePay ransomware gang ‘among most active’ with more than 600 victims since 2024
last_week_digest.tldr: The SafePay ransomware syndicate has compromised over 600 organisations across Europe and the Americas since 2024, causing severe operational disruptions and significant financial liabilities, including an 80 million dollar settlement. This surge signals a shift toward aggressive extortion tactics, highlighting critical vulnerabilities in global infrastructure and the escalating professionalisation of cybercrime.

last_week_digest.title: Russian GRU hackers hit NATO shipbuilder, aircraft engine maker, law enforcement agency in espionage campaign
last_week_digest.tldr: Russian GRU-linked hackers recently compromised a naval shipbuilder, an aircraft engine manufacturer, and a law enforcement agency across NATO nations. This espionage campaign, utilising advanced backdoors, signals a persistent, targeted threat to the global defence industrial base, highlighting how state-sponsored actors are aggressively prioritising intelligence collection against critical military supply chains.

last_week_digest.title: Zeabur shutting down after second security breach in two months
last_week_digest.tldr: Development platform Zeabur is shutting down following a second major security breach in two months. Attackers exploited plaintext credentials to compromise 321,810 accounts and 3.2 million environment records. This collapse signals that failing to rotate administrative access and secure internal infrastructure after initial incidents creates unsustainable operational risks for modern providers.

last_week_digest.title: AOMEI Backupper Compromised in Short-Burst Supply Chain Campaign
last_week_digest.tldr: AOMEI Backupper suffered multiple supply chain compromises, exposing 186 million global users to malware via short-burst server tampering. Threat actor UNC7017 exploited unauthenticated update configurations to deploy backdoors across various sectors. This incident signals an evolving, opportunistic shift towards transient, harder-to-detect delivery methods, forcing organisations to prioritise rigorous integrity verification for software updates.

last_week_digest.title: Children’s Data Stolen After Ransomware Attack Compromises ‘Password1’ Account
last_week_digest.tldr: Ransomware attackers breached Data Cymru’s network using a weak ‘Password1’ credential, exposing personal data of 3,300 people, mostly children. This incident highlights how poor third-party oversight and legacy account management create severe operational risks, signalling that basic authentication hygiene remains a critical global vulnerability.

last_week_digest.title: CISA: Hackers chain Plex flaws in Plex2Shell attacks to breach servers
last_week_digest.tldr: Attackers are actively chaining four critical Plex Media Server vulnerabilities, rated 9.8, to achieve remote code execution. This wave of exploitation, alongside Siemens and SiteGuard breaches, highlights a growing industry trend where attackers bypass perimeter defenses, forcing organisations to accelerate patching cycles to prevent compromise.

last_week_digest.title: FBI and CISA Warn of SafePay Ransomware Attacks on 600 Organizations
last_week_digest.tldr: SafePay ransomware has compromised over 600 global organisations since August 2024, leveraging stolen credentials and VPN vulnerabilities to execute double-extortion attacks. This surge signals a shift toward independent, non-affiliate threat actors, forcing businesses to prioritise robust identity management and edge device security against sophisticated, persistent threats.

last_week_digest.title: Meta Ordered to Pay New Mexico $25 Billion for Deceiving Users About Privacy on Facebook
last_week_digest.tldr: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion for deceiving users regarding data privacy, citing over 43 million legal violations. This record-breaking penalty highlights a growing global trend of aggressive state-level enforcement, signaling that tech giants face increasing financial risks for misleading practices.

last_week_digest.title: Democrat lawmakers say Russia is aiming to undermine party ahead of midterms
last_week_digest.tldr: Senior lawmakers report that Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea are deploying sophisticated disinformation campaigns to erode voter confidence ahead of US elections. While direct infrastructure hacking remains absent, these influence operations signal a permanent shift toward destabilising democratic institutions, forcing businesses to navigate heightened geopolitical volatility.

last_week_digest.title: Microsoft Links ConnectWise Breach to China-Linked Group Using AI Pentesting Tool ARTEX
last_week_digest.tldr: The China-linked group Storm-0940 compromised 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants by exploiting ConnectWise credentials via the AI-driven ARTEX framework. This attack achieved privileged cloud access in under three hours, signalling a shift toward machine-speed supply chain exploitation. Organisations must now audit service principal credentials, as malicious persistence often survives the remediation of initial compromised applications.

last_week_digest.title: Iranian Hacking Group Found Hosting C2 Infrastructure in the US
last_week_digest.tldr: The Iranian threat group Prince of Persia is utilising US-based command-and-control infrastructure to facilitate cyber-espionage, marking the first such occurrence in twelve years. By deploying sophisticated malware like Tornado, the group exfiltrates sensitive data from global organisations. This development signals a strategic shift, highlighting how adversaries exploit domestic hosting providers to bypass traditional security perimeters.

last_week_digest.title: New PHP2Shell scanner checks your hosts for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619
last_week_digest.tldr: Searchlight Cyber released an open-source scanner to detect two critical PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities affecting platforms like WordPress and Magento. By triggering memory-exhaustion conditions, the tool identifies exploitable hosts that traditional version-based scanners miss. This development signals a shift toward active, risk-based testing, highlighting the urgent need for robust patching across global web infrastructures.

last_week_digest.title: 11 Million Impacted by Capcom Data Breach
last_week_digest.tldr: Capcom recently suffered a significant data breach exposing 11,774,247 email addresses and personal records through its CAPCOM ID service. While operational services remain functional, the incident forces a costly reputational recovery and mandatory security overhaul. This breach signals a growing trend where global gaming giants face heightened risks regarding massive, centralised user database vulnerabilities.

last_week_digest.title: Cybercrime crackdown across Africa leads to 1,462 arrests, $105 million seized
last_week_digest.tldr: Operation Serengeti III, an Interpol-led crackdown across twenty African nations, resulted in 1,462 arrests and the recovery of $105 million in illicit funds. By disrupting 10,000 malicious networks, authorities addressed $385 million in losses affecting 66,000 victims. This significant intervention signals a growing global commitment to dismantling transnational fraud rings and organised cybercrime syndicates.

last_week_digest.title: SECURITY AFFAIRS MALWARE NEWSLETTER ROUND 120
last_week_digest.tldr: Recent malware campaigns, including supply chain attacks on LiteLLM and hijacked OVHcloud CLI releases, highlight a significant escalation in targeted digital threats. These incidents expose critical vulnerabilities in software development pipelines, threatening operational integrity and data security globally. This trend signals that organisations must urgently prioritise robust supply chain auditing to mitigate persistent, sophisticated risks.

last_week_digest.title: Capcom Data Breach Exposes 11.7 Million Email Addresses
last_week_digest.tldr: Capcom confirmed a significant data breach involving its CAPCOM ID service, exposing 11,774,247 email addresses and associated account metadata globally. While services remain operational, the incident forced password resets for 196 compromised accounts. This breach highlights the persistent vulnerability of large-scale gaming platforms to unauthorised access, signalling an urgent need for enhanced identity security.

last_week_digest.title: Widespread Token-Spraying Attacks Target Microsoft 365 Accounts For Email Compromise
last_week_digest.tldr: A widespread campaign targeting Microsoft 365 environments utilised token-spraying to bypass multi-factor authentication, resulting in 497 successful account compromises across 79 organisations. By stealing session tokens, attackers gained persistent access to corporate networks, enabling fraudulent email activity. This development signals a shift toward sophisticated identity-based attacks that render traditional authentication methods insufficient for global enterprises.

last_week_digest.title: In Other News: Tor Exit Relays Hijacked, Banks Spot Rogue AI Agents, Self-Rebuilding macOS Ransomware
last_week_digest.tldr: Recent cyber incidents include an $80 million settlement for Conduent’s 2024 data breach and Bullhorn forcing credential resets following a platform hack. Meanwhile, investigators linked a consulting executive to the ShinyHunters extortion ring, and new ISO/IEC standards now address AI data poisoning. These events signal that supply chain vulnerabilities and AI-driven threats require urgent attention.

last_week_digest.title: Quest Diagnostics warns of potential data theft after attack on lab service system
last_week_digest.tldr: Quest Diagnostics suspended its Quanum Lab Services Manager platform following unauthorized access, potentially exposing sensitive patient data. This operational disruption forces healthcare providers to revert to manual processes, highlighting the fragility of critical medical infrastructure. The incident signals a growing trend of targeted cyberattacks against healthcare firms, prompting stricter global regulatory oversight and compliance.

last_week_digest.title: Magento Campaign Infects 953 Online Stores Across Five Domains
last_week_digest.tldr: A sophisticated skimming campaign has compromised 953 Magento online stores since July 2025, using advanced bot-filtering techniques to evade security scanners. This persistent threat highlights significant vulnerabilities in e-commerce content management systems, signalling an urgent need for robust integrity monitoring to protect global consumer data.

last_week_digest.title: Gheist Attackers Stumble in Attempt to Abuse GitHub Tokens
last_week_digest.tldr: The Gheist campaign compromised 850 accounts, injecting malicious workflows across 13,500 GitHub branches to harvest sensitive credentials. While platform controls mitigated public repository risks, private enterprise environments remain exposed, signalling that stolen tokens continue to weaponise legitimate automation features against global supply chains.

last_week_digest.title: Ukraine warns hackers are exploiting Chinese-made Dahua surveillance cameras
last_week_digest.tldr: Ukrainian cybersecurity authorities warn that hackers are exploiting vulnerabilities in Dahua surveillance cameras to compromise over 14,500 devices. This breach, enabling remote access to sensitive video feeds, highlights critical supply chain risks and signals an urgent need for global organisations to prioritise firmware security.

last_week_digest.title: Energy giant ENGIE discloses data breach affecting customers
last_week_digest.tldr: French energy giant ENGIE confirmed a data breach involving a third-party marketing platform, exposing contact details and contract information for French customers. This incident highlights the critical operational risk posed by partner-managed tools, signalling that supply chain vulnerabilities remain a primary target for global enterprises.

last_week_digest.title: Stolen AI Reasoning Could Help China Build Cheaper Rivals
last_week_digest.tldr: Chinese entities have systematically extracted billions of tokens from Western frontier AI models to train rival systems through distillation. This exploitation of API reasoning traces threatens intellectual property, signalling that securing proprietary model architectures is now a critical operational priority for global technology firms.

last_week_digest.title: Japan's GMO urges customers to shut down PCs amid ransomware threat
last_week_digest.tldr: Japan’s GMO Internet Group faces a severe crisis after hackers breached its Onamae Desktop Cloud, potentially compromising 26,739 servers. The firm refused a $50 million ransom demand, leading to data leaks and urgent customer shutdowns. This incident highlights the critical vulnerability of cloud infrastructure to credential-based attacks and extortion threats.

last_week_digest.title: Three Japan-Focused Cyberattacks Show How Hackers Use AI
last_week_digest.tldr: Three cyberattacks targeting nineteen organisations in Japan demonstrate how hackers leverage AI to automate reconnaissance and exploit legacy systems. These incidents, including one using forty-four AI agents, signal a shift toward scalable, low-traffic attacks. This evolution forces global businesses to prioritise securing public-facing infrastructure against increasingly efficient, AI-driven threat actor operations.

last_week_digest.title: External Teams Chats Anchor 15-Minute Malware Delivery
last_week_digest.tldr: Black Basta affiliates are exploiting Microsoft Teams’ external chat functionality to deliver malware within fifteen minutes of initial contact. This social engineering campaign targets global organisations, bypassing traditional security perimeters to facilitate ransomware deployment. The attack signals a critical shift toward abusing trusted enterprise collaboration tools to accelerate operational disruption.

last_week_digest.title: Nefilim, Hive ransomware operator given five-year-plus sentence after guilty plea
last_week_digest.tldr: Artem Stryzhak, a prolific ransomware affiliate, received a 70-month prison sentence for attacks against hospitals and government entities across 80 countries. His activities, involving both Nefilim and Hive groups, caused over $100 million in losses. This prosecution signals a growing global commitment to dismantling ransomware syndicates through multi-continent legal cooperation.

last_week_digest.title: Secrets Management Firm Infisical Valued at $600 Million After $40 Million Raise
last_week_digest.tldr: Secrets management firm Infisical has secured $40 million in Series B funding, reaching a $600 million valuation. Serving 1,300 organisations including Airbus and Volkswagen, the company aims to mitigate risks posed by AI agents. This investment signals that securing machine-to-machine credentials is now a critical priority for global enterprise cybersecurity strategies.

last_week_digest.title: GhostAction Hacking Wave Fizzles, But Attackers Lurk on in GitHub
last_week_digest.tldr: The GhostAction campaign targeting developer endpoints and cloud infrastructure highlights a growing shift toward supply chain exploitation. By infiltrating GitHub repositories, attackers threaten global software integrity, forcing organisations to rethink security protocols as these persistent threats signal a broader, dangerous evolution in cybercrime tactics.

last_week_digest.title: 345,000 email addresses stolen in cyberattack on Germany’s far-right party AfD
last_week_digest.tldr: A cyberattack on Germany’s AfD party exposed 345,000 email addresses, compromising internal communications and sensitive voter data. This breach highlights significant vulnerabilities in political IT infrastructure, signalling that organisations must urgently prioritise robust security protocols to protect against politically motivated data exfiltration and reputational damage.

last_week_digest.title: Volt Typhoon hides zero-day attacks using 'Silent Train' framework
last_week_digest.tldr: The state-sponsored group Volt Typhoon is utilising the Silent Train framework to launch stealthy zero-day attacks against critical global infrastructure. By rotating compromised relay devices, the actors maintain persistent access, signalling a shift toward highly evasive, targeted operations that threaten operational continuity for international enterprises.

last_week_digest.title: Japan Airlines warns of data breach as country grapples with multiple cyber incidents
last_week_digest.tldr: Japan Airlines confirmed a data breach at IT provider Amadeus, exposing personal records of 92,000 customers. This incident, alongside millions of records stolen from other Japanese firms, signals a systemic vulnerability in third-party supply chains, prompting urgent government intervention to bolster national cybersecurity resilience.

last_week_digest.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit PHP2Shell to Root Firewalls
last_week_digest.tldr: China-linked hackers exploited critical PHP vulnerabilities to compromise 24 firewalls, eventually infiltrating a government-affiliated management server to harvest credentials and domain data. This targeted operation highlights a growing trend of nation-state actors weaponising edge device flaws to gain persistent, high-level access to internal networks.
